fields.description:
Remove the deprecated force_close INPUT surface so the write-op parity oracle needs zero exceptions. Operator ruling (2026-08-18): remove deprecated flags/verbs rather than exempt or mirror them. force is the sanctioned gate-bypass across all surfaces; force_close is its deprecated predecessor.

## Context / Problem
Keeping force_close as an accepted INPUT would force the parity oracle to carry an exception (or mirror a dead flag onto MCP just to match). Removing the input surface lets the oracle assert total parity with no allow-list. The surviving force=True path already covers the operator use case force_close served (a closed-without-signed-attestation audit signal).

## Approach
Retire force_close as an accepted INPUT on the lib and CLI ONLY, routed through the supported rebar._deprecations warn/tombstone path. CRITICAL event-sourcing caveat: force_close is not only an input — it also lives in the event schema + reducer (schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, reducer/_processors_status.py, _commands/txn.py, transition_close.py, close_precheck.py, types.py). This is an event-sourced store, so historical events carrying force_close MUST keep reducing to the same state. This is therefore a tombstone of the INPUT surface, NOT a hard delete: the reducer and schema keep tolerating historical force_close events unchanged.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_lib_writes.py — remove force_close as an accepted transition() input param; warn-tombstone it via rebar._deprecations.
- src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py (and the close disposition/precheck input path) — remove the CLI force_close input spelling; warn-tombstone.
- src/rebar/_deprecations.py — register the force_close input tombstone.
- Reducer/schema (reducer/_processors_status.py, schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, _commands/txn.py, types.py) — INTENTIONALLY UNCHANGED for historical-event tolerance.
- Sweep the lib/CLI/MCP write verbs for any other deprecated input flag that would otherwise require an oracle exception; record findings on the ticket.

## Testing
- Passing force_close as an input emits a rebar._deprecations warning and is no longer an accepted param (unit test asserts the warning and that it is not honored as a live bypass).
- A fixture event stream carrying a historical force_close event still reduces to the identical ticket state (reducer back-compat test).
- The parity oracle (sibling topaz-blubbery-mice) carries no force_close row/exception and still passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Passing force_close as an input WARNs via rebar._deprecations and is no longer a supported live param (unit test).
- [ ] Docs and docstrings no longer advertise force_close as a usable input (grep is clean).
- [ ] A historical event carrying force_close still reduces to the same ticket state (reducer fixture test passes).
- [ ] The parity oracle carries no force_close exception and passes.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green.
